hook.curiosityMechanism: Most viewers assume their paycheck already reflects their real earnings — withholding quietly says otherwise.
hook.viewerQuestion: Why does your paycheck never match your full salary?
hook.payoffExpectation: Viewers will understand what withholding is and how to check their own numbers.

beats.purpose: Open with the gap between salary and take-home pay.
beats.expectedViewerState: Curious about why their paycheck looks smaller than expected.

beats.purpose: Explain the withholding mechanism and preliminary survey data about common errors.
beats.expectedViewerState: Understands why paychecks are reduced and that many first-time filers misjudge withholding.
beats.qualification: Early filing data suggests about 30% of first-time filers misjudge withholding; the figure may shift as the season continues.

beats.purpose: Ground the explanation in the IRS's own public statement.
beats.expectedViewerState: Trusts that fixing withholding errors is achievable.

beats.purpose: Invite the viewer to subscribe for the next explainer.

payoff.description: Viewers leave understanding why their paycheck differs from their salary and trusting that withholding mistakes are fixable.

conclusion.summaryApproach: Recap the withholding mechanism and reassure viewers that checking their own numbers is straightforward.
conclusion.finalTakeaway: Understanding withholding turns a confusing paycheck into a predictable one.

ctaStrategy.rationale: Viewers who want to understand their paycheck are a good match for future explainer content.

claims.claimText: Federal income tax withholding reduces an employee's paycheck before net pay is deposited, which is why take-home pay is lower than gross salary.
Early filing data suggests that about 30% of first-time filers underestimate their federal withholding.
limitations: Based on early-season survey data only; may not hold for the full filing season.
claims.notesForDownstream: Present as an early/preliminary figure, not a final result.

claims.claimText: Most withholding errors are simple to fix once you know where to look.
